####################################################################################################
Purpose of script: This script produces descriptive statistics and various plots (maps, histograms, 
density plots) based on the final data sets (s08). It creates visual summaries of study 
participants, study locations, vaccination dates, immunogenicity measurements, and additional maps 
for selected pathogens.

Functions Used:
- `fun_breaks.R`: Function to set nice upper, middle, and lower breaks in ggplot.
- `fun_limits.R`: Function to set nice upper, and lower limits in ggplot.

Outputs:
Saved in the /figures directory:
- `data_raw_individuals.pdf` Participant information ("Who?")
- `data_raw_map.pdf` Locations of randomized controlled trials ("Where?")
- `data_raw_vaccinations.pdf` Dates when vaccinations were administered ("When?")
- `data_raw_immunogenicity_time.pdf` Time interval between the last vaccination and immunogenicity 
   measurement ("When AB?")
- `data_raw_immunogenicity.pdf` Immunogenicity measurements after vaccination ("What?")

For each selected pathogen (14 in total):
- `map_reg_6_{i}.pdf` Maps showing RCT locations for each pathogen.

Additionally, a combined figure for the manuscript is saved as:
- `fig1.pdf`
####################################################################################################

# Load packages, themes, directories, and functions
```{r}
rm(list = ls())
source("00_pck.R")
source("fun_figures/fun_breaks.R")
source("fun_figures/fun_limits.R")
library(colorspace)
theme_set(theme_classic())
```

# Read in the data (only s08 data)
```{r}
dat_l <- lapply(str_subset(list.files(glue("{dirs$modfit}"), full.names = TRUE), "s08.rds"), readRDS)
names(dat_l) <- sub(".*brms_(.*?)_(vl|v1)_s08.*", "\\1", 
                    str_subset(list.files(glue("{dirs$modfit}")), "s08.rds"))
```

# Summary Statistics: Basic checks on participants, studies, and countries
```{r}
# Check 96 studies and 48599 participants
length(unique(bind_rows(dat_l, .id = "pat")$pid))
length(unique(bind_rows(dat_l, .id = "pat")$study))
# Number of countries
length(unique(bind_rows(dat_l, .id = "pat")$country))
# Summary 
select(bind_rows(dat_l, .id = "pat"), country, age, vac_date_v1, lat_med, lon_med, time_v1_v2, 
       time_v2_v3, time_vl_s1) %>%
  summary()
```

# Plot 1 – "Who?": Participant Information
```{r}
# Extract participants information and merge all data sets. 
df_pl1 <- bind_rows(lapply(dat_l, distinct, study, pid, sex, age), .id = "pat") %>%
  # Add tidy names for the pathogens 
  left_join(pat_tidy_names, by = join_by(pat)) %>%
  # Create a new variable ('mod') categorizing the pathogens.
  mutate(mod = case_when(str_detect(pat, "multi", negate = TRUE) ~ "UVN unipathogen",
                         pat %in% c("multi_ipv", "multi_men", "multi_opv", "multi_pertua",
                                    "multi_strep") ~ "MVN unipathogen",
                         pat %in% c("multi_dtpa", "multi_dtpw", "multi_hib-men",
                                    "multi_mmr", "multi_mmr-vzv") ~ "MVN multipathogen"))

# Plots --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Plot 1.1: Histogram of participants per pathogen and study (with number of studies as label)
pl1.1 <- ggplot(df_pl1, aes(y = fct_rev(pat_tidy), group = study, fill = mod)) +
  geom_bar(aes(group = mod), stat = "count", color = "white", size = 0.1) + 
  geom_bar(stat = "count", color = "white", fill = "transparent", size = 0.1) + 
  geom_label(data = distinct(df_pl1, pat_tidy, study, pid) %>%
               group_by(pat_tidy) %>%
               summarise(study_tot = length(unique(study)), tot = n()), 
             aes(x = tot + 800, y = fct_rev(pat_tidy), label = as.character(study_tot)), 
             color = "grey50", fill = "transparent", size = 2, inherit.aes = FALSE) + 
  scale_x_continuous("Total vaccinated individuals", expand = c(0,0), limits = c(0,22500)) +
  scale_y_discrete("") + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("orange", "dodgerblue", "darkblue")) + 
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_line())

## Plot 1.2: Age at Vaccination (Histogram and Density)
pl1.2 <- ggplot(df_pl1, aes(x = age/4, y = fct_rev(pat_tidy), color = mod)) +
  geom_point(shape = "|", size = 4, alpha = 0.1) +
  scale_x_continuous("Age at first vaccination (months)", 
                     breaks = c(0, 2, 4, 6, 12, 18, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72, 84), expand = c(0,0)) +
  scale_y_discrete("") + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("orange", "dodgerblue", "darkblue")) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("orange", "dodgerblue", "darkblue")) + 
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        axis.line.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_line())

## Plot 1.3: Sex Ratio by Pathogen (Stacked Bar Chart) (dark is males, light is females)
pl1.3 <- ggplot(df_pl1, aes(y = fct_rev(pat_tidy), fill = mod, alpha = sex)) +
  geom_bar(color = "white", position = "fill") + 
  scale_x_continuous("Sex proportion", breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1), expand = c(0,0)) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("orange", "dodgerblue", "darkblue")) + 
  scale_alpha_discrete(range = c(0.1, 1)) + 
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        axis.line.y = element_blank())

## Patch plots together
pl1 <- pl1.1 + pl1.2 + pl1.3 + plot_layout(widths = c(3,6,1))

# Save the plot 
ggsave(pl1, file = glue("{dirs$figures}/data_raw_individuals.pdf"), width = 9.5, height = 8)
```

# Plot 2 – "Where?": Study Locations Map
```{r}
# Prepare data for the plot 
## Read in world map data (polygon outlines for country boundaries)
world <- map_data("world") 
## Prepare location data: For non-multi pathogen studies, extract unique locations and count 
## the number of individuals per country (using median latitude/longitude)
df_pl2 <- bind_rows(lapply(dat_l[str_subset(names(dat_l), "multi", negate = TRUE)], function(x) {
  # Obtain the number of individuals per location in a country
  distinct(x, pid, country, lat_med, lon_med) %>%
    group_by(country, lat_med, lon_med) %>%
    summarise(tot = n(), .groups = "drop")
  }), .id = "pat") %>%
  # Add tidy names for the pathogens 
  left_join(pat_tidy_names, by = join_by(pat)) %>%
  # Rename countries to match world map
  mutate(country = case_when(country == "United States" ~ "USA", .default = country))

# Plot it ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
pl2 <-ggplot() +
  # Add latitude lines and polygons (dark for countries included in the study)
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = c(-35, -23.5, 0, 23.5, 35)), linewidth = 0.5, color = "grey85") + 
  geom_polygon(data = world, aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group), fill = "grey90") +
  geom_polygon(data = filter(world, region %in% c(unique(as.character(df_pl2$country)))), 
               aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group), fill = "grey75") + 
  # Add points of the locations 
  geom_point(data = df_pl2, aes(x = lon_med, y = lat_med, color = pat_tidy, size = tot), alpha = 0.8) + 
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = df_pl2, aes(x = lon_med, y = lat_med, 
                                              color = pat_tidy, label = pat_tidy),
                           alpha = 0.8, max.overlaps = 15) + 
  scale_y_continuous("Latitude (°)", 
                     breaks = c(-35, -23.5, 0, 23.5, 35), limits = c(-60,80), expand = c(0,0)) +
  scale_x_continuous("Longitude (°)", expand = c(0,0)) + 
  scale_color_viridis_d(name = "Vaccination") +
  scale_size_continuous("Total vaccinated \nindividuals",
                        breaks = c(500, 1500, 2500), limits = c(1,5000)) + 
  guides(size = guide_legend(title.position = "top", nrow = 5, byrow = T),
         color = guide_legend(title.position = "top", nrow = 5, byrow = T),
         shape = "none") +
  theme_void() + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey", colour = "white"),
        strip.text = element_text(colour = "white"),
        panel.grid = element_blank()) + 
  coord_quickmap()

# Save the plot 
ggsave(pl2, file = glue("{dirs$figures}/data_raw_map.pdf"), width = 15, height = 15)
```

# Plot 3 – "When?": Vaccination Week Information
```{r}
# Prepare data for the plot 
df_pl3 <- bind_rows(lapply(dat_l, distinct, study, pid, vac_week_v1, age, reg_6), .id = "pat") %>%
  # Add tidy names for the pathogens 
  left_join(pat_tidy_names, by = join_by(pat)) %>%
  # Change names of the models 
  mutate(reg_6 = as.character(reg_6))

# Plot it ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Plot 3.1: Histogram of Vaccination Weeks (by Pathogen and Study)
pl3.1 <- ggplot(group_by(df_pl3, pat, study, vac_week_v1) %>%
                  mutate(tot = n()), 
                aes(x = vac_week_v1, fill = study)) +
  geom_histogram(color = "transparent", size = 0.1, bins = 52) + 
  facet_wrap(pat_tidy~., scales = "free_y", ncol = 5) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d() +
  scale_x_continuous("Week of vaccination", breaks = c(1, 18, 35, 52), expand = c(0,0)) + 
  scale_y_continuous("", breaks = fun_breaks, limits = fun_limits, expand = c(0,0)) + 
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none")

## Plot 3.2: Scatter Plot of Vaccination Week by Region
pl3.2 <- ggplot(group_by(df_pl3, pat, reg_6, vac_week_v1) %>%
                  mutate(tot = n()), 
                aes(x = vac_week_v1, y = reg_6, color = reg_6, alpha = tot)) +
  geom_point() + 
  facet_wrap(pat_tidy~., ncol = 5) +
  scale_x_continuous("Week of vaccination", breaks = c(1, 18, 35, 52), expand = c(0,0)) + 
  scale_y_discrete("", limits = rev) + 
  scale_color_viridis_d() +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none")

## Patch plots together
pl3 <- pl3.1 + pl3.2 + plot_layout(ncol = 1)

# Save the plot 
ggsave(pl3, file = glue("{dirs$figures}/data_raw_vaccinations.pdf"), width = 10, height = 19)
```

# Plot 5 – "What?": Immunogenicity Measurements After Vaccination
```{r}
# Prepare data for the plot 
## Multi pathogen or multi immunogenicity to long format 
df_pl5 <- sapply(filter(pat_tidy_names, pat %in% names(dat_l))$pat, function(x) {
  ## If not multi, just distinct 
  if(str_detect(x, "multi") == FALSE) { 
    distinct(dat_l[[x]], study, pid, imm_val_s1, imm_sero_s1, imm_met_s1, imm_cutoff_s1, age)
  ## If multi, select and pivot 
  } else { 
    select(dat_l[[x]], study, pid, age, 
           starts_with("imm_val_s1"), starts_with("imm_met_s1"), starts_with("imm_cutoff_s1")) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("imm_"), names_to = c(".value", "imm_sero_s1"), 
                 names_pattern = "^(imm_[a-z]+_s1)_(.*)$")
  }
}, simplify = FALSE)

## Handle missing immunogenicity methods and merge tidy pathogen names
df_pl5 <- sapply(names(df_pl5), function(x) {
  if(!any(str_detect(names(df_pl5[[x]]), "imm_met_s1"))) {
    mutate(df_pl5[[x]], 
           imm_met_s1 = case_when(!is.na(imm_val_s1) ~ unique(dat_l[[x]]$imm_met_s1)),
           pathogen = x) %>%
      # Add tidy names for the pathogens 
      left_join(pat_tidy_names, join_by(pathogen == pat))
  } else {
    mutate(df_pl5[[x]], pathogen = x) %>%
      # Add tidy names for the pathogens 
      left_join(pat_tidy_names, join_by(pathogen == pat))
  }  
}, simplify = FALSE)

# Plot it ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
pl5_l <- list()
for(i in names(df_pl5)) {
  pl5_l[[i]] <- filter(df_pl5[[i]], !is.na(imm_val_s1)) %>%
    mutate(imm_sero_s1 = str_remove(imm_sero_s1, "anti_"),
           imm_name_met = as.character(glue("{imm_sero_s1} ({imm_met_s1})"))) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = imm_val_s1, fill = study)) +
    geom_histogram(color = "transparent", bins = 30) + 
    facet_wrap(imm_name_met~., scales = "free", dir = "v", ncol = 5) +
    scale_x_continuous("Immunogenicity", expand = c(0,0), trans = "log10") +
    scale_y_continuous(unique(df_pl5[[i]]$pat_tidy), expand = c(0,0)) + 
    scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "") + 
    theme(legend.position = "none", 
          strip.background = element_blank())
}
## Patch plots together
pl5 <- wrap_plots(pl5_l) + plot_layout(ncol = 3)

# Save the plot 
ggsave(pl5, file = glue("{dirs$figures}/data_raw_immunogenicity.pdf"), width = 16, height = 40)
```

# Figure 1 =========================================================================================

# Figure 1a ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare data for the plot 
```{r}
# Define selected pathogens for the manuscript figure
pat_sel <- c("rota", "hav", "hbv", "dipht", "tetan", "pertuapt", "ipv1",
             "hib", "menc", "strep04", "measl", "mumps", "rubel", "vzv")

# Prepare data for Figure 1a: Combine participant data for the selected pathogens and 
# merge with tidy pathogen names.
df_fig1a <- bind_rows(lapply(dat_l[pat_sel], distinct, study, pid, sex, age), .id = "pat") %>%
  # Add tidy names for the pathogens 
  left_join(pat_tidy_names, by = join_by(pat))
```

# Figure 1a Plots: Participants, Age, and Sex Ratio
```{r}
## Figure 1a.1: Histogram showing the number of participants per study for each pathogen
fig1a.1 <- df_fig1a %>%
  # Obtain number of participants per study 
  group_by(pat, pat_tidy, study) %>%
  summarise(tot = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Obtain proportion of participants per pathogen
  group_by(pat, pat_tidy) %>%
  arrange(pat, tot) %>%
  mutate(tot_prop = tot/sum(tot)) %>%
  # Plot
  ggplot(aes(y = fct_rev(pat_tidy), x = tot, group = reorder(study,tot), fill = tot_prop)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "white", size = 0.1) + 
  geom_label(data = distinct(df_fig1a, pat_tidy, study, pid) %>%
               group_by(pat_tidy) %>%
               summarise(study_tot = length(unique(study)), tot = n()), 
             aes(x = tot + 800, label = as.character(study_tot), y = fct_rev(pat_tidy)), 
             fill = "white", color = "grey50", inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 2) + 
  scale_x_continuous("Total vaccinated individuals", expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 22500)) +
  scale_y_discrete("") + 
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "rocket", trans = "log") + 
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_line())

## Figure 1a.2: Plot showing age at first vaccination (in months) by pathogen
fig1a.2 <- df_fig1a %>%
  # Obtain age in weeks 
  mutate(age = round(age/4, digits = 0)) %>%
  # Obtain number of individuals per age  
  group_by(pat_tidy, pat, age) %>%
  summarise(tot = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Plot
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = fct_rev(pat_tidy), size = tot, color = tot)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.9) + 
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "rocket", trans = "log", end = 0.9) + 
  scale_x_continuous("Age at first vaccination (months)",
                     breaks = c(0, 2, 4, 6, 12, 18, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72, 84)) +
  scale_y_discrete("") + 
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        axis.line.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_line())

## Figure 1a.3: Stacked bar plot showing the sex ratio by pathogen
fig1a.3 <- ggplot(df_fig1a, aes(y = fct_rev(pat_tidy), fill = sex)) +
  geom_bar(color = "white", position="fill") + 
  scale_x_continuous("Sex proportion", breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1), expand = c(0,0)) + 
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "rocket", begin = 0.6, end = 0.9) + 
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        axis.line.y = element_blank())

## Patch plots together 
fig1a <- fig1a.1 + fig1a.2 + fig1a.3 + plot_layout(widths = c(3,4,0.5))
```

# Figure 1b: Maps and additional density plots for selected pathogen -------------------------------

# Prepare data for the plot 
```{r}
## Read in world map 
## Read in world map data (polygon outlines for country boundaries)
world <- map_data("world") 

## Prepare data for two groups of selected pathogens, merging tidy names and 
## standardizing country names (e.g., "United States" to "USA")
df_fig1b1 <- bind_rows(dat_l[pat_sel[1:7]], .id = "pat") %>%
  left_join(pat_tidy_names, by = join_by(pat)) %>%
  mutate(country = case_when(country == "United States" ~ "USA", .default = country))
df_fig1b2 <- bind_rows(dat_l[pat_sel[8:14]], .id = "pat") %>%
  left_join(pat_tidy_names, by = join_by(pat)) %>%
  mutate(country = case_when(country == "United States" ~ "USA", .default = country))

## Aggregate location data across all selected pathogens for mapping purposes
df_ple <- bind_rows(lapply(dat_l[pat_sel], function(x) {
  distinct(x, pid, country, reg_4, reg_6, lat_med, lon_med) %>%
    group_by(country, reg_4, reg_6) %>%
    summarise(tot = n(),
              lat_med = mean(lat_med),
              lon_med = mean(lon_med), 
              .groups = "drop")
  }), .id = "pathogen") %>%
  # Add tidy names for the pathogens 
  left_join(pat_tidy_names, join_by(pathogen == pat)) %>%
  # Rename countries to match world map
  mutate(country = case_when(country == "United States" ~ "USA", .default = country))
```

# Plot it

## Figure 1b.1: Time-series plots of vaccination weeks per region
```{r}
fig1b.1.1 <- df_fig1b1 %>%
  # Obtain total participants per week and region
  group_by(pat, pat_tidy, vac_week_v1, reg_4) %>%
  summarise(tot = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(pat, pat_tidy) %>%
  complete(vac_week_v1, reg_4, fill = list(tot = 0)) %>%
  # Plot
  ggplot(aes(x = vac_week_v1, y = tot, color = reg_4)) +
  geom_step() +
  facet_wrap(.~pat_tidy, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous("Week of vaccination", breaks = c(1, 18, 35, 52), expand = c(0,0)) +
  scale_y_continuous("Count", breaks = fun_breaks, limits = fun_limits, expand = c(0,0)) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "mako", begin = 0.2, end = 0.8) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(hjust = 0),
        legend.position = "none") 
fig1b.1.2 <- df_fig1b2 %>%
  # Obtain total participants per week and region
  group_by(pat, pat_tidy, vac_week_v1, reg_4) %>%
  summarise(tot = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(pat, pat_tidy) %>%
  complete(vac_week_v1, reg_4, fill = list(tot = 0)) %>%
  # Plot
  ggplot(aes(x = vac_week_v1, y = tot, color = reg_4)) +
  geom_step() +
  facet_wrap(.~pat_tidy, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous("Week of vaccination", breaks = c(1, 18, 35, 52), expand = c(0,0)) +
  scale_y_continuous("Count", breaks = fun_breaks, limits = fun_limits, expand = c(0,0)) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "mako", begin = 0.2, end = 0.8) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(hjust = 0),
        legend.position = "none") 
```

# Figure 1b.3: Maps of study locations for each subgroup of pathogens
```{r}
fig1b.3.1 <- bind_rows(lapply(unique(df_fig1b1$pat), function(x) {
  mutate(world, 
         pat = x,
         dat = case_when(region %in% (filter(df_fig1b1, pat == x))$country ~ TRUE, .default = FALSE)
         )})) %>%
  # Add tidy names for the pathogens 
  left_join(pat_tidy_names, by = join_by(pat)) %>%
  # Plot 
  ggplot(aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group, fill = dat)) +
  facet_grid(pat_tidy~.) +
  geom_polygon() +
  geom_point(data = filter(df_ple, pathogen %in% df_fig1b1$pat),
             aes(x = lon_med, y = lat_med, color = reg_4, size = tot, group = 1, fill = NA), 
             alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous("Longitude (°)", expand = c(0,0)) + 
  scale_y_continuous("Latitude (°)", 
                     breaks = c(-23.5, 0,23.5), limits = c(-60,80), expand = c(0,0)) +
  scale_size_continuous("Total vaccinated \nindividuals",
                        breaks = c(500, 1500, 2500), limits = c(1,5000)) + 
  scale_color_viridis_d(name = "Vaccination", option = "mako", begin = 0.2, end = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey90", "grey75")) + 
  guides(size = guide_legend(title.position = "top", nrow = 3, byrow = T),
         color = guide_legend(title.position = "top", nrow = 3, byrow = T),
         shape = "none") +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank()) + 
  coord_quickmap()
  
fig1b.3.2 <- bind_rows(lapply(unique(df_fig1b2$pat), function(x) {
  mutate(world, 
         pat = x,
         dat = case_when(region %in% (filter(df_fig1b2, pat == x))$country ~ TRUE, .default = FALSE)
         )})) %>%
  # Add tidy names for the pathogens 
  left_join(pat_tidy_names, by = join_by(pat)) %>%
  # Plot 
  ggplot(aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group, fill = dat)) +
  facet_grid(pat_tidy~.) +
  geom_polygon() +
  geom_point(data = filter(df_ple, pathogen %in% df_fig1b2$pat),
             aes(x = lon_med, y = lat_med, color = reg_4, size = tot, group = 1, fill = NA), 
             alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous("Longitude (°)", expand = c(0,0)) + 
  scale_y_continuous("Latitude (°)", 
                     breaks = c(-23.5, 0,23.5), limits = c(-60,80), expand = c(0,0)) +
  scale_size_continuous("Total vaccinated \nindividuals",
                        breaks = c(500, 1500, 2500), limits = c(1,5000)) + 
  scale_color_viridis_d(name = "Vaccination", option = "mako", begin = 0.2, end = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey90", "grey75")) + 
  guides(size = guide_legend(title.position = "top", nrow = 3, byrow = T),
         color = guide_legend(title.position = "top", nrow = 3, byrow = T),
         shape = "none") +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank()) + 
  coord_quickmap()
```

# Figure 1b 
```{r}
## Patch plots together 
fig1b <- fig1b.1.1 + fig1b.2.1 + fig1b.3.1 + fig1b.1.2 + fig1b.2.2 + fig1b.3.2 + 
  plot_layout(nrow = 1, widths = c(0.75,0.75,2,0.75,0.75,2))
```

```{r}
## Patch plots together 
fig1 <- free(fig1a) + fig1b + plot_layout(nrow = 2, heights  = c(1,2))

# Save the plot 
ggsave(glue("{dirs$figures}/fig1.pdf"), width = 12, height = 10)
```

# Per-Pathogen Maps: Create individual maps for each selected pathogen =============================

# Prepare data for the plot 
```{r}
# Combine data for selected pathogens and standardize country names
df_figmaps <- bind_rows(dat_l[pat_sel], .id = "pat") %>%
  left_join(pat_tidy_names, by = join_by(pat)) %>%
  mutate(country = case_when(country == "United States" ~ "USA", .default = country))
```

# Generate and Save a Map for Each Pathogen
```{r}
# Create a color palette for regions
col_lat <- viridis::mako(length(unique(df_figmaps$reg_6)), begin = 0.2, end = 0.8)
names(col_lat) <- sort(as.character(unique(df_figmaps$reg_6)))

pl_l <- list()
## Map of study locations 
for (i in unique(df_figmaps$pat)) {
pl_l[[i]] <- mutate(world,
         pat = i,
         dat = case_when(region %in% (filter(df_figmaps, pat == i))$country ~ TRUE, .default = FALSE)
         ) %>%
  # Add tidy names for the pathogens 
  left_join(pat_tidy_names, by = join_by(pat)) %>%
  # Plot 
  ggplot(aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group, fill = dat)) +
  facet_wrap(pat_tidy~., ncol = 4) +
  geom_polygon() +
  geom_point(data = filter(df_ple, pathogen == i),
             aes(x = lon_med, y = lat_med, color = as.character(reg_6), size = tot, group = 1, fill = NA), 
             alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous("Longitude (°)", expand = c(0,0)) + 
  scale_y_continuous("Latitude (°)", 
                     breaks = c(-23.5, 0,23.5), limits = c(-60,80), expand = c(0,0)) +
  scale_size_continuous("Total vaccinated \nindividuals",
                        breaks = c(500, 1500, 2500), limits = c(1,5000)) + 
  scale_color_manual(name = "Vaccination", values = col_lat) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey90", "grey75")) + 
  guides(size = guide_legend(title.position = "top", nrow = 3, byrow = T),
         color = guide_legend(title.position = "top", nrow = 3, byrow = T),
         shape = "none", fill = "none") +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank()) + 
  coord_quickmap()

  # Save each pathogen-specific map to file
  ggsave(pl_l[[i]], file = glue("{dirs$figures}/map_reg_6_{i}.pdf"), width = 10, height = 5)
}
```
